title: Quantum Barankin bounds beyond local unbiasedness: Analytic results for Gaussian states via a right-division framework
authors: Maximilian Reichert, Javier Navarro, Gerardo Adesso, Manuel Gessner, Mikel Sanz
abstract: We propose a quantum version of the Barankin bound as an alternative to the quantum Cramér-Rao bound for quantum parameter estimation. The quantum Barankin bound provides a lower bound on the mean squared error of estimators satisfying arbitrarily chosen bias constraints at arbitrarily chosen parameter points. In particular, unbiasedness over the entire parameter space can be imposed, yielding precision limits for globally unbiased quantum parameter estimation. In contrast to the recently derived quantum Barankin bound, which is based on a symmetric division superoperator, our bound is based on a nonsymmetric right-division superoperator. This formulation enables us to find analytic expressions for the Barankin matrix for Gaussian states, which allows for an efficient calculation of the bound. We demonstrate the usefulness of our results by applying them to various examples that exhibit the threshold effect in the few-shot regime, which is invisible to the standard quantum Cramér-Rao bound approach.
summary: This work introduces a quantum Barankin bound, a tighter lower bound on estimation error than the standard QCRB, by utilizing a non-symmetric right-division framework. The authors provide analytic formulas for this bound specifically for Gaussian states. This offers a more powerful tool for determining the ultimate precision limits in quantum parameter estimation, particularly in few-shot regimes.
main_problem: The paper proposes a quantum generalization of the Barankin bound as an alternative to the Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound (QCRB) for quantum parameter estimation.
main_result: They derive a novel, non-symmetric quantum Barankin bound using a right-division superoperator, which is shown to be generally tighter than previous symmetric bounds.
method: The methodology involves extending classical estimation theory bounds to the quantum domain, deriving explicit analytic formulas for Gaussian states using matrix algebra and characteristic functions.

key_observables: Mean Squared Error (MSE) of estimators, Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and the Barankin matrix.
important_parameters: The parameter set $\Lambda$ and the specific structure of the Gaussian states (defined by mean vectors and covariance matrices).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the existence and properties of the right-division superoperator and the assumption that the relevant operators are trace class.
paper_structure: The paper develops the bound by first establishing the general framework using the right-division operator, comparing it to the symmetric version, and then specializing the results to derive analytic formulas for Gaussian states.
why_interesting: The development of tighter, analytically tractable bounds for parameter estimation is crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum measurements, especially in regimes where standard QCRB fails.
